Author: Subhash Chandra Sharma
Bench: Subhash Chandra Sharma
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 80
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 6394 of 2022
Applicant :- Rohit Jaiswal

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :-
Atul Kumar Shahi Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Lalji Yadav,Yashpal Yadav Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Short counter affidavit filed today by learned counsel for opposite party no. 2 is taken on record.

Heard Sri Anoop Trivedi, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Sri Atul Kumar Shahi, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Yashpal Yadav, learned counsel for opposite party no. 2 as well as Sri Shivdatta Shukla, learned A.G.A. for State and perused the record.

Facts in brief are that the informant belonged to scheduled caste and was preparing for competitive examination at Rapti Nagar, Phase-3 and was teaching in private school & tuition to meet her expenses.
Anjana Sharma was principal in U.S. Central Academy, Sikriganj, Gorakhpur who came into the contact and told her that there was need of a teacher in her school.
She went to the school for employment and started teaching from August, 2018.

The president of school Rohit Jaiswal (this applicant) opened new branch of school at Kaudiram where Anjana Sharma was deputed as principal and the informant was sent there for publicity of the branch.

On 22.3.2019 when the Rohit Jaiswal vs State Of U.P. And Another on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60524976/
1 informant came back in her staff room and was taking rest alone, the applicant entered into the room and said that her qualification was good and assured her to provide Government Job and started making conversation on phone.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Later on, on 25.4.2019 he called her to Delhi with the documents of her qualification where she went to his room and on 26.4.2019 in the night intoxicated cold drink was provided to her and then the applicant committed rape with her by force and also prepared video.

He also threatened her to make her video viral in case, she would make complaint to the police, thereafter he committed rape with her by force under the threat of making the video viral, then she left the school, even though the applicant committed rape with her under threat that he would make video viral and took her to Varanasi in a hotel then at Delhi and Rapti Nagar and when she objected such act of the applicant, he insulted her by using words related to her caste and also threatened that in case if she will not establish physical relations with him, her video would be made viral and she will be abducted and murdered.

As a result the informant and her family came under fear due to which she lodged this F.I.R. on 15.4.2020 against this applicant under Sections 376, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3(2)(V) of S.C./S.T. Act and Section 66-E I.T. Act which was challenged before this Court and was disposed of with the direction to provide protection in favour of the applicant till submission of police report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C.
During investigation the material was collected and statement of victim was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
After conclusion of investigation charge sheet was submitted under Sections 376, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3(2)(V) of S.C./S.T. Act and Section 66-E I.T. Act.

On 27.11.2020 against which an application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. was moved before this Court which was dismissed vide order dated 31.5.2022 after considering all the facts and submissions made on the part of the applicant against which the applicant moved a Special Leave Petition before the Hon'ble Apex Court which was also dismissed.
Then the present anticipatory bail application has been moved before this Court.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
Informant was a married lady and was in relation with the applicant prior to the alleged incident.
There was chatting between both of them which shows that they were in love affair.
When relations between both of them became strained, she lodged this F.I.R. against him with false allegations.
Further submitted that though charge sheet was challenged u/s 482 Cr.P.C. before this Court and it was dismissed but the anticipatory bail application is to be decided on merits of the case.

From the allegation in the F.I.R. and material collected during investigation,
no offence under S.C./S.T. Act is made out against him, therefore, anticipatory bail application is maintainable in relation to the offence said to be committed by the applicant against the informant.
The applicant was not the manager of the school but his father was manager, therefore, the allegation made by the informant in this case is false.
It is also submitted that the statement made by the victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C. does not inspire confidence though she has reiterated the version made by her in the F.I.R.
No any sign was found on the person of the victim during medical examination to indicate forceful sexual assault.
The allegation about adverse caste remark is also not clear from the bare reading of the F.I.R.
It is further submitted that applicant was ready to provide his blood sample but the opposite party/informant refused from giving her sample.
During investigation, it was found that on the alleged dates the location of the applicant was found on different places.

In this way it is established that applicant is innocent and has committed no offence rather he has been threatened and Rohit Jaiswal vs State Of U.P. And Another on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60524976/
2 blackmailed by the opposite party no. 2.

sentences.text:
Since he was provided protection during investigation of the case and made cooperation with the investigation, now, after submission of charge sheet,
cognizance has been taken by the learned court, therefore apprehension of arrest is arisen against the applicant in pursuance of the process of the court.

On the other hand, learned counsel for opposite party no. 2 as well as learned AGA opposed the prayer of anticipatory bail and urged that in this case, there is allegation in the F.I.R. made by the informant against this applicant to commit rape with her on the pretext of providing employment and also prepared video by threatening her of making it viral.
Applicant committed rape with her several times on several places.
The victim has narrated the whole story even before the learned Magistrate who recorded her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
The applicant challenged the F.I.R. in which his submission and the allegations were considered by this Court and it was dismissed as having no force.

During investigation, sufficient material was collected by the Investigating Officer on the basis of which prima facie case was found established under Section 376, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3(2)(V) of S.C./S.T. Act and Section 66-E I.T. Act against the applicant.

Further urged that charge sheet has been submitted against him, which was also challenged before this Court but after considering all the facts and circumstances of the case and material on record and submissions made on the part of the applicant, it was also dismissed.
Now the court has taken cognizance of the offences against the applicant on the basis of material on record which shows that applicant has committed the offence as aforesaid.

It is also urged that since the offence under Section 3(2)(V) S.C./S.T. Act is also made out therefore, as per Section 18(A)2 of S.C./S.T. Act, the anticipatory bail application u/s 438 Cr.P.C. cannot be entertained.

In this way,
the applicant is not entitled for anticipatory bail.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for opposite party no. 2 as well as learned A.G.A. and perusal of record, it appears that in this case the allegation of rape, use of words relating to the caste of the informant, threat and also preparing video was made against this applicant in the aforesaid F.I.R.
which was found to be established during investigation and prima facie case under Section 376, 504,
506 IPC and Section 3(2)(V) of S.C./S.T. Act and Section 66-E I.T. Act. was found to be established and learned court concerned has also taken cognizance of the offence under the Act and the bar under Section 18-A(2) of S.C./S.T. Act, there appears no ground to grant indulgence in favour of this applicant.

The anticipatory bail application of applicant Rohit Jaiswal involved in Case Crime No. 69 of 2020, under Sections 376, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3(2)(V) of S.C./S.T. Act and Section 66-E I.T.
Act, P.S. Bansgoan, District Gorakhpur is hereby rejected.
